failure_patterns.pattern: answer_format: Returned a longer, narrower, or differently inflected form than the expected canonical answer (lamprey, Napoleon, radical, pineapples).

rejected_edits.content: - For a clue-style fragment, first identify the requested answer slot, then treat each stated attribute and relation as a constraint. Reject candidates that match only the broad topic or role but fail a distinctive fact or an explicit category, ingredient, or other qualifier. In a biographical statement, return the person described by the subject or pronoun, not an office or organization mentioned in the predicate. When snippets compete, prefer evidence that fits the full clue over keyword overlap, prominence, or a similar name; do not substitute a related entity, example, remedy, or mechanism.
rejected_edits.target: - Before answering, parse the requested answer slot and all identifying relations or properties, then test the candidate against the complete clue. When snippets compete, prefer factual evidence that fits those details; keyword overlap in a title or heading, prominence, or a similar name alone is not enough. Do not substitute a related entity, example, remedy, or mechanism for the requested answer.

rejected_edits.content: - Use the context-supported conventional form of a name or answer, and include additional name parts only when needed to distinguish otherwise-confusable entities. In an English-language clue, prefer an established English name over a source-language alias unless the prompt requests the original-language form. When the clue asks you to identify an entity, return its name alone rather than a phrase restating the property or formula used to identify it.
rejected_edits.target: - Use the context-supported conventional form of a name or answer, and include additional name parts only when needed to distinguish otherwise-confusable entities.
